claims.text: Advanced free-energy sampling can guide NM-HEA synthesis.
Free-energy-sampling guidance will enable simultaneous control of alloying and dealloying during NM-HEA formation.
Controlled alloying and dealloying will produce three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
The resulting nanoframeworks will have a more uniform atomic distribution.
The proposed precursor is a homogeneous, well-mixed, stoichiometric blend of noble-metal ions or atoms.
Free-energy sampling can map the barriers associated with alloying and dealloying.
Free-energy calculations can be used to select temperature, laser-pulse, or chemical-reduction parameters during synthesis.
Multi-element alloying and concurrent dealloying can occur under the proposed thermal or pulsed-laser synthesis regimes.
Free-energy barriers mediate transitions between alloyed and dealloyed states.
Control of those barriers governs the development of a porous, interconnected three-dimensional nanoframework.
Mapping the free-energy landscape permits precise tuning of synthesis parameters to favor simultaneous alloying and controlled dealloying.
Simultaneous alloying and controlled dealloying lead to atomic-scale uniformity among the noble metals.
Simultaneous alloying and controlled dealloying lead to an interconnected, porous three-dimensional nanostructure.
Free-energy-guided synthesis will yield better-defined three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks than conventional synthesis.
Free-energy-guided synthesis will improve atomic-scale homogeneity relative to conventional synthesis.
Improved nanoframework definition and atomic-scale homogeneity will enhance catalytic performance.
Conventional precursor-mixing methods typically produce less-controlled atomic distributions.
Conventional precursor-mixing methods typically produce suboptimal porous frameworks.
